'''Margaret Smagorinsky''' (23 December 1915 – 14 November 2011) was an American statistician, computer programmer, and weather technologist.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Witman |first=Sarah |date=2017-06-16 |title=The Unheralded Contributions of Klara Dan von Neumann |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/meet-computer-scientist-you-should-thank-your-phone-weather-app-180963716/ |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref> She was the first female statistician hired by the [[National Weather Service|United States Weather Bureau]].

== Early life ==

Smagorinsky was born in [[Brooklyn]], New York, as the second of four daughters of Anne and George Knoepfel. She attended [[Bay Ridge High School]] in Brooklyn.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Obituary information for Margaret Smagorinsky |url=https://www.matherhodge.com/obituaries/Margaret-Smagorinsky?obId=27303234 |website=The Mather-Hodge Funeral Home |language=en-US}}</ref>

Smagorinsky was the first member of her family to attend college when she attended [[Brooklyn College]]. She graduated at age 19 with a degree in mathematics, and taught school in a one-room schoolhouse in Ashland, New York, for four years.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |first1=Kristine |last1=Harper |author1-link=Kristine C. Harper|last2=Doel |first2=Ronald |date=2006-01-02 |title=Transcript of Oral History Interview of Margaret Smagorinsky |url=https://opensky.ucar.edu/islandora/object/archives%3A7644?search_api_fulltext=smagorinsky |website=American Meteorological Society University Corporation for Atmospheric Research}}</ref>

== Statistics career ==
Smagorinsky took the [[United States Civil Service Commission|civil service exam]] for a statistical clerk in the US. She was offered a job at the [[Railroad Retirement Board]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], where she worked as a statistician processing paperwork for employees looking to enter the civil service.

At age 26, Smagorinsky joined the Weather Bureau, where she was the first woman statistician.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=1943-07-11 |title=Weather Bureau's 1st girl statistician hails from Boro |pages=7 |work=The Brooklyn Daily Eagle |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/114740647/weather-bureaus-1st-girl-statistician/ |access-date=2022-12-17}}</ref> After being sent to [[New York University]] for additional coursework,<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://archive.org/details/newdictionaryofs0006unse |title=New dictionary of scientific biography |date=2008 |location=Detroit  |publisher= Charles Scribner's Sons/Thomson Gale |isbn=978-0-684-31320-7 |pages=470|volume=6|editor-last=Koertge|editor-first=Noretta}}</ref> she met [[Joseph Smagorinsky]] in a graduate statistics course. He was 8 years her junior, and they married on May 29, 1948.<ref name=":0" />

Smagorinsky had five children: Anne, [[Peter Smagorinsky|Peter]], Teresa, Julia, and Frederick. She left full-time government employment after her first child was born in 1951.{{Citation needed|date=April 2023}}

Smagorinsky, in supporting her husband's work, processed data and programmed the [[ENIAC]] (Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer).<ref name=":2">{{Citation |last=Smagorinsky |first=Joseph |chapter=The Beginnings of Numerical Weather Prediction and General Circulation Modeling: Early Recollections |date=1983-01-01 |chapter-url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0065268708601703 |title=Advances in Geophysics |volume=25 |pages=3–37 |editor-last=Saltzman |editor-first=Barry |access-date=2023-03-05 |series=Theory of Climate |publisher=Elsevier |doi=10.1016/S0065-2687(08)60170-3 |bibcode=1983AdGeo..25....3S |isbn=978-0-12-018825-3 |language=en|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> In April 1950, a group of meteorologists at New Jersey's [[Institute for Advanced Study]] successfully produced the first weather forecast using the ENIAC and numerical prediction techniques.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Nebeker |first=Frederik |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sYEBl7QfqS0C&dq=%E2%80%9Clift+the+veil+from+previously+undisclosed+mysteries+connected+with+the+science+of+weather+forecasting%2C%E2%80%9D&pg=PA137 |title=Calculating the Weather: Meteorology in the 20th Century |date=1995 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-08-052841-0 |language=en|pages=137}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Dyson |first=George |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6sElRNGXWFIC&dq=Margaret+Smagorinsky&pg=PA166 |title=Turing's Cathedral: The Origins of the Digital Universe |date=2012 |publisher=Pantheon Books |isbn=978-0-375-42277-5 |pages=166 |language=en}}</ref> Smagorinsky is cited as a programmer of computers for 5-day weather forecast models created by the Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory at the [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]].<ref name=":2" />
